headline: High-risk pair: Cursor’s broad filesystem/network/MCP access can leak or corrupt workflow data when paired with Prefect orchestration, with default-path prompt injection and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs; Prefect can move workflow metadata through API-driven orchestration. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in shared files or task outputs can be treated as instructions. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Cursor reads Prefect-generated files or logs as instructions
IF an MCP server or shared workspace carries untrusted content between the agents
mitigations: Disable MCP access for the shared workspace
Separate Prefect outputs from Cursor-opened files
Mark workflow artifacts as untrusted in review notes
Use read-only copies for any Prefect logs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and has broad network egress; Prefect handles workflow metadata and also has broad egress. If they share a local filesystem or clipboard, sensitive code or metadata can flow from Cursor into Prefect-managed artifacts or outbound requests. The shared-workspace path is explicit in Cursor’s profile, while Prefect’s outbound surface makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF Cursor and Prefect share a local filesystem or clipboard
IF Prefect tasks upload workflow artifacts containing code or secrets
mitigations: Keep Cursor and Prefect on separate workspaces
Clear clipboard before running Prefect tasks
Restrict Prefect artifact uploads for sensitive runs
Use redacted copies of code in shared folders
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; Prefect can also act on shared mutable resources through orchestration and API-driven workflows. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git changes can collide without locking. Because Cursor’s default session shares state via local filesystem, the conflict path is dangerous by default and can corrupt work or commits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Prefect-triggered tasks and Cursor edits overlap in time
mitigations: Pause Prefect runs during Cursor editing sessions
Use separate git branches per agent
Add a manual lock file before writes
Limit Cursor to read-only mode for shared repos
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code, commands, or facts from workspace context, and Prefect is an orchestration system that can consume those outputs as workflow inputs. If Prefect treats Cursor output as authoritative, a single hallucinated or malformed artifact can cascade into automated downstream actions. The pair’s default automation makes this a high-risk failure mode.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes Cursor-produced files, prompts, or metadata without verification
IF downstream Prefect workflows trigger actions based on those inputs
mitigations: Require human review of Cursor outputs before Prefect use
Validate schemas on all handoff files
Add checksum checks between agents
Disable auto-triggered Prefect actions for AI-generated artifacts
requires-engineering: implement provenance and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while Prefect is open-source and primarily touches workflow metadata. If regulated data is placed in Cursor and then propagated into Prefect workflows or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is edited in Cursor and then exported into Prefect workflows
IF organizational policy requires different retention or residency handling for code versus workflow metadata
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Review retention settings for Prefect runs
Use separate projects for sensitive workflows
Redact identifiers before handoff
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
